subject: PrivDeploy canonical-stack review and CI merge-gate plan
body:
From: Sally Tran <sally.tran@acme-cloud.com>
To: rishi_malhotra, marissa_cole, kimberly_park
Cc: J. Lee <j.lee@edgeops.io>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: ACME: Priv deploy IaC review - canonical stack draft

Hi team,

Thanks again for taking this on. Attached is the first draft of ACME's private deployment IaC (Terraform modules + Helm charts + small Ansible bootstrap) and a network diagram. High-level asks:

- Quick pass for obvious security or compliance gaps we should close before we hand this to ACME procurement (evidence they will expect).
- Recommendations for CI merge-gates we can add to prevent configuration drift (what to require in a merge vs. what can be gated post-merge).
- Any module ownership / artifact signing gaps you see.

Attachments: acme-priv-iac-draft.patch, priv-network-diagram.png

Sally
ACME Cloud - Platform PM

----

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.example.com>
To: Sally Tran <sally.tran@acme-cloud.com>, marissa_cole, kimberly_park
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 11:03:12 -0800
Subject: Re: ACME: Priv deploy IaC review - canonical stack draft

Thanks Sally — received and skimmed. Quick take before we dig into the patch:

- We should treat this as both an IaC review and a minimal evidence collection exercise. Procurement will want provenance (signed chart tarballs and a basic artifact index).
- CI merge-gates: blocking pipeline jobs I recommend upstream of merge: terraform validate & fmt, terraform plan with diff upload, policy-check (OPA/Conftest) against policies repo, and a chart-sign step for Helm charts. Post-merge jobs can include deeper integration tests in a canary namespace (see Marissa's note below).
- Network: the diagram shows a NAT egress node per-environment which is fine, but we need explicit egress allowlists and a documented fallback for regional peering failures (routing policy).

Can everyone add line-item comments in the attached merge-gate-proposal.md and I'll consolidate? I'll schedule a 30 min sync for Thursday morning.

Rishi
Director, Product Infra
Redwood Inference

Attachments: merge-gate-proposal.md

----

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>
To: rishi_malhotra, Sally Tran <sally.tran@acme-cloud.com>
Cc: kimberly_park, dev_patel
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 08:47:35 -0800
Subject: Re: ACME: Priv deploy IaC review - canonical stack draft

Quick notes after a short pass on the patch and diagram:

- Helm: default values.yaml currently enables nodePort for the admin service. Recommend switch to ClusterIP + explicit ingress mapping so that customers don't accidentally open admin ports.
- Terraform modules: add REQUIRED output describing module_owner and artifact_digest (SLSA-lite) for every published module. This will simplify evidence packaging.
- Canary namespace: add a GitLab CI job that deploys to a namespaced canary for 1 hour and runs smoke checks (model-serving health + metrics). If smoke checks fail, block rollout to prod.
- Logging: recommend a short list of retention windows (30/90/365) and where logs will be archived for audit. Add these to the evidence folder on the Drive link.

Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C_privdeploy_evidence

Marissa
Sr. PM, Infra Reliability

----

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.example.com>
To: rishi_malhotra, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Sally Tran <sally.tran@acme-cloud.com>, dev_patel
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 15:30:05 -0800
Subject: Re: ACME: Priv deploy IaC review - canonical stack draft

Adding procurement/compliance lens:

- Procurement will ask for module ownership statements and an evidence bundle for each version. We should produce a canonical tarball per release (signed) and a short manifest that maps module versions to provenance.
- We'll also need a minimal SOC2-ish mapping for network controls (egress allowlists, VPC flow logs, retention). I can draft a one-pager and attach to the Drive folder.
- Looping in dev_patel to validate CI feasibility and to make sure the githooks/merge-gates are implementable with our current GitLab setup.

Kimberly
Head of Security & Compliance

----

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.example.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.example.com>, rishi_malhotra, marissa_cole
Cc: Sally Tran <sally.tran@acme-cloud.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 10:05:20 -0800
Subject: Re: ACME: Priv deploy IaC review - canonical stack draft

Technical checklist (actionable items I can take on / prototype this week):

- Terraform: enforce terraform fmt and terraform validate in pre-merge. Require plan to be uploaded as pipeline artifact named "tf-plan.json". Add a small parser task that detects any delta in network.routed_subnets and egress_rules and flags for manual review.
- Modules: require module metadata in registry (module_owner, artifact_digest, source_repo, signed_by). Add a job to verify chart tarball signatures using cosign.
- Helm: add chart sign/verify step in build stage. If chart verification fails, fail the pipeline.
- Ansible: use ansible-vault for secrets; ensure vault password is not checked in and pipeline reads from KMS at runtime.
- OPA/Policy: run conftest/opa against both terraform plan JSON and Helm templates. Policy repo should be pinned by commit SHA in pipeline config.
- CI merge-gates: proposed minimal required jobs to pass before merge: fmt, validate, tf-plan-upload, policy-check, chart-sign-verify. Post-merge: canary-deploy -> smoke-tests -> promote job.
- Network specifics: propose adding a CI check that validates private route tables include at least one NAT gateway or egress proxy and that no 0.0.0.0/0 open security groups are present.

I can push a prototype pipeline (GitLab CI YAML) to the sample repo PRIVDEP-templates and attach to drive. Need access to proceed with chart-sign key.

Dev
Senior Infra Engineer

Attachments referenced: sample-gitlab-ci.yml (in Drive)

----

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.example.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.example.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Sally Tran <sally.tran@acme-cloud.com>, ACME Procurement <procure@acme-corp.com>, J. Lee <j.lee@edgeops.io>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 15:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ACME: Priv deploy IaC review - canonical stack draft

Great progress everyone — summary and next steps:

1) Merge-gate definition (agreed minimal set pre-merge): terraform fmt, terraform validate, tf-plan upload, policy-check (OPA/Conftest), chart-sign-verify. If any of these fail, block merge.
2) Post-merge: run canary-deploy (1 hour) + automated smoke-tests. If smoke-tests fail, auto-trigger rollback and open an incident card.
3) Evidence bundle: Marissa/Kim to produce module ownership manifests and a signed artifact tarball. Dev to provide cosign verification job.
4) Network controls: add pipeline check for egress allowlists and explicit NAT/proxy config; add a documented fallback routing policy for peering outages (Marissa to draft).

Action owners and rough ETA:
- Dev Patel: prototype GitLab CI (tf plan uploader, policy-check, chart-sign verify) — ETA 2026-11-27
- Marissa Cole: canary test job + smoke check spec — ETA 2026-11-24
- Kimberly Park: procurement one-pager + evidence manifest template — ETA 2026-11-24
- Rishi: schedule dry-run window with ACME (aiming week of 2026-12-06) and consolidate merge-gate-proposal.md into the Drive folder.

Sally: can you confirm procurement's timeline for evidence acceptance? If they need anything sooner we can reprioritize the prototype.

Thanks — will follow up with a calendar invite for the dry-run planning sync.

Rishi
Director, Product Infra
Redwood Inference
